conflicts.description: The Cartographers warn that the bridges are dying, but the other enclaves suspect Solenne of seeking control over the archipelago.
conflicts.name: The Failing Skybridges

conflicts.description: The Windwrights' tolls and the Weavers' need for free trade threaten any shared effort to mend the skybridges.
conflicts.name: The Storm Lane Rivalry

conflicts.description: The Echo Keepers hold the verses that could rekindle the skybridges but fear that revealing them will repeat old mistakes.
conflicts.name: The Hidden Verses

description: Aerelune is a wondrous, fractured realm of floating islands drifting in a luminous sky, once held in a single constellation by ancient skybridges woven from starlit stone and living light. Now the skybridges are failing, and the archipelago slowly loosens toward the open sky. Rival enclaves guard their own islands, their own crafts and their own grievances, and few believe the danger is real. Mara Quillfeather, a young cartographer, charts the drifting islands and discovers that the skybridges are dimming in a pattern that points toward a coming separation. This is a fantasy of hope and discovery for young adults, where maps, music and mending matter more than conquest. To save Aerelune, Mara must carry the truth between enclaves that distrust each other, and persuade them to rekindle the skybridges together before the islands drift beyond reach.

factions.description: Mapmakers of Solenne who record the drift of every island and the state of every skybridge. They are respected but are often dismissed as dreamers.
factions.name: The Cartographers' Hall

factions.description: Artisans who spin luminous thread and believe skybridges must be mended with craft and patience.
factions.name: The Miravel Weavers

factions.description: Engineers and kite-ship captains who control the storm lanes and consider the oldest skybridge their rightful charge.
factions.name: The Ondrelle Windwrights

factions.description: Memory-singers of Lirael who hold the lost verses needed to wake the skybridges, and share them only with those they trust.
factions.name: The Echo Keepers

history.description: The founders sang the first skybridge between Solenne and Lirael, binding the islands into one archipelago.
history.name: The Raising of the First Span

history.description: A plague of forgetting led the Echo Keepers to seal away the verses of the chorus, and the knowledge of rekindling was withdrawn.
history.name: The Silencing of the Verses

history.description: Ondrelle began charging tolls for storm-lane passage, souring relations with Miravel's merchants.
history.name: The Storm Toll Dispute

history.description: A skybridge near Miravel flickered and faded, an event the enclaves dismissed as a passing fault.
history.name: The First Dimming

locations.description: The sunlit central island of terraced gardens and glass observatories, home to the Cartographers' Hall. Its great skybridge anchors connect to every other island.
locations.name: Solenne

locations.description: A misty island of silver orchards and singing wind-chimes, where weavers tend the fibers that once reinforced each skybridge.
locations.name: Miravel

locations.description: A stormy island of waterfalls that pour into the sky, ruled by proud engineers and sailors of kite-ships who guard the oldest skybridge span.
locations.name: Ondrelle

locations.description: A quiet, crystalline island of echoing caves and archives, where the memory-keepers preserve songs describing how the first skybridge was raised.
locations.name: Lirael

name: Aerelune

rules.statement: Every skybridge is sustained by living light, and its brightness holds neighboring islands in place.
When a skybridge dims past a threshold, its two islands begin to drift apart at a steady pace.
A skybridge can be rekindled only by a chorus of voices from at least three enclaves singing together.
Aerelune's craft relies on wind, thread, glass and light, and no explosive weapons exist since the fragile skybridges would shatter under them.
Anyone crossing a skybridge is granted safe passage, and violating it is the gravest offense among the enclaves.
